result:
Solution 1 is wrong. Its key step, that $\beta(\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}) = 2^n$, fails because a faithful $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-orbit of size $2^n$ is a regular antichain, and the paragraph's construction doesn't rescue it. A direct check also rules out $2^n+2$ for $G=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$. Any element of order 2 not in every order-4 subgroup forces an orbit of size $2^n$ with kernel $\langle X\rangle$ or $\langle Z\rangle$. The only other orbit(s) then total 2 points. That gives at most 4 types of elements in the big antichain, so two elements of the same type are twins. Swapping them is an automorphism that is not in $G$, since nontrivial elements of $G$ fixing those two extra points move every point of the big orbit.

Solution 2 is wrong. Its claim that the minimum equals $3\cdot 2^n$ is not derived. Its orbit-kernel argument does not establish a lower bound of that size, and the construction is asserted rather than verified.

Solution 3 is wrong. Its construction requires $S = S + 2^{n-1}$, which makes $c_i$ and $c_{i+2^{n-1}}$ twins (same up-sets, both minimal and incomparable). Transposing them is an extra automorphism outside $\langle\sigma,\tau\rangle$, so the automorphism group is strictly larger than $G$. The lower bound $2^{n+1}$ is also unproven, so the value $2^{n+1}$ is not established.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
